question: A toy store started with 27 figures in stock. In February inventory tripled to 81 figures. In March it multiplied by 8 more. The store restocked 37 additional figures. By year-end seasonal sales multiplied the total fivefold. The store's competitor had 89 figures. How many figures did the toy store have by year-end?

Alice started the game Monday with 239 points. By morning she earned 34 points. At midday she earned 71 more. In the afternoon she earned 68 additional. By evening she earned 75 more challenge points. Her brother Bob had 156 points separately. In the final tournament Alice's score multiplied by 4. How many points did Alice end with?

A student read 78 pages Monday. Tuesday she read 5 times Monday's amount. Wednesday she read 5 times Tuesday's amount. Thursday she tripled Wednesday's amount. A comprehension check made her reread exactly half of this total. By Sunday she added 79 more pages. She had a notebook with half a dozen bookmarks saved. How many total pages had she read?

Sarah had 40 dollars Monday morning. She spent 14 dollars on breakfast. She earned 37 dollars at work. She spent 2 dollars on a snack. Her remaining amount then doubled for commission purposes. How much did she have after commission?

A warehouse had 107 boxes Monday morning. By afternoon they received 31 boxes. By evening they received 37 more. Tuesday morning 64 more arrived. By evening 57 additional boxes were delivered. The warehouse manager had worked there 12 years. How many total boxes did they have?

A bookstore started with 237 manuscripts. They rejected 52 initially. The remainder was divided equally among 5 editors. 30 were returned for revisions. 5 more were rejected after review. The selected ones were expanded into 4 language editions. How many manuscripts were finally approved?

Sarah started with 26 dollars. She earned 40 dollars that week. These were multiplied by 5 through bonuses. Tax withholding then halved this amount. She spent 103 on equipment. She earned 4 more in tips. Tom earned 80 dollars. How much did Sarah have remaining?

A restaurant served 73 customers daily. Over 4 weeks this was their standard load. Each week has 7 operating days. One day 18 extra customers came. A promotion brought 70 additional customers. The owner's brother's restaurant served 200 daily. How many total customers did they serve?

Sarah started with 33 apples. She gave 22 to a neighbor. She picked 40 more bringing her to 51. She multiplied sales orders by 5 requesting 255 apples. Supply limits halved this to 51 per shipment. Her friend Jane wanted 20 apples. What was Sarah's final shipment quantity?

A farm produced 54 bushels day 1. Day 2 multiplied by 8 to 432. Day 3 multiplied by 7 to 3024. Day 4 multiplied by 9. A neighboring farmer contributed 67 bushels. They harvested a dozen apple trees that week. How many total bushels did they accumulate?

A company started with 25 units. Q1 multiplied by 4 to 100 units. Q2 multiplied by 5 to 500. Q3 multiplied by 6 reaching 3000. Q4 sold 2461 units. A competitor made 800 units that quarter. How many units remained at year-end?

A teacher had 201 students across classes. She dismissed 157 leaving 44. A new program multiplied classes by 7 requiring 308 students. She moved 299 to electives. Those remaining doubled for evening sessions. How many students attended evening classes?

A mechanic started with 139 tools in his shop. He organized and removed 95 broken tools. He then acquired 26 new tools from an estate sale. He added 15 more tools from a colleague. He then added 53 tools from a supplier order. His apprentice borrowed 18 tools for a project, which weren't included in the total. What was his final tool inventory?

A student had 81 minutes of homework time available. By morning, 72 minutes had been used. By afternoon, she gained 3 minutes of free time. By evening, she completed 39 more minutes of work. She then lost 10 minutes to a phone call. Her study buddy had 25 minutes of homework (tracked separately). How many minutes of homework time remained?

A factory produced 233 units daily. This was multiplied by 9 through shift increases. They added 4 units from quality improvements. They then subtracted 2055 units for a major recall (converting lost units to replacement calculation). They multiplied by 9 for the following month's projections. Her coworker managed a separate line with 18 units. What was the monthly projection?

A publisher had 216 pages of manuscript. They divided by 4 for four separate chapters. Each chapter was then multiplied by 8 for editing passes. It was then multiplied by 8 again for final review stages (measured in total review units). The final pages per chapter total were divided by 2 for PDF layout conversion. One editor proofread 10 pages independently (extra work). What was the final layout count?

A chef started prep with 39 ingredient portions. He subtracted 18 portions for prep waste. This was then multiplied by 4 for serving batches. It was then multiplied by 8 for dining room tables. He subtracted 39 portions for staff meals. The final count was divided by 3 for plating distribution. His sous chef prepared 7 extra portions (tracked separately). David and Rachel will compare their portion counts at service. What was the portion distribution per plate?

A student took a test starting with 128 points. In section one, they lost 67 points. In section two, they lost 5 more points. In section three, they gained 69 points. In section four, they gained 75 points. Throughout the exam, they moved through morning, afternoon, and evening sessions. One problem was worth 12 bonus points (not included in the main calculation). What was their final test score?

A runner began with 80 miles of training. She lost 7 miles during an injury week. She lost 61 more miles due to illness. This was multiplied by 4 for training intensity. It was multiplied by 6 again for competition preparation. She subtracted 164 miles from a recalculation error. She added 73 miles from additional sessions. Throughout the training, she progressed from morning runs to afternoon sprints and evening recovery. Her coach assigned 22 miles for special training (separate). What was her final training mileage?

A manufacturing plant produced 198 items daily. It was multiplied by 6 through increased staffing. It was multiplied by 6 again for expanded shifts. They added 6 items from quality improvements. They subtracted 6073 items for a product recall (converting to adjusted production). They subtracted 92 items for defect removal. They subtracted 676 items for a market adjustment. At least one item was produced as a sample (though included in totals). What was the adjusted production count?

A student had 218 pages to read. He added 65 pages from supplementary materials. This was multiplied by 4 for study cycles. He subtracted 1091 pages for topics already covered. He subtracted 38 more pages from curriculum changes. Throughout his studies, he progressed from morning reviews through afternoon intensive study to evening reflection. His textbook had 156 pages that were reference only (not part of the count). What was his final required reading?

A collector started with 142 rare coins. She multiplied by 6 for auction lot calculation. She subtracted 687 coins from a price correction. This was multiplied by 5 for collection value. She added 79 coins from an inheritance. She added 41 more coins from purchases. Michael and Susan each had comparable collections for evaluation. David had 23 coins in his collection (separate). How many coins did the final collection contain?

A builder started with 134 work items on the checklist. He multiplied by 7 for the number of construction phases. He added 50 items from quality checks. He added 6 items from safety reviews. He added 19 items from final inspections. Throughout the build, work progressed from morning framing through afternoon finishing and evening documentation, with work items tracked at each phase. His assistant completed 8 items early. What was the total work item count?

A runner completed 98 miles in training. By morning practice, he'd subtracted 89 miles as a baseline. By afternoon, he subtracted 1 mile from adjustment. By evening, he subtracted 3 more miles. By final tally, he subtracted 1 mile from a timing error. He then multiplied his remaining effort by 7 for weekly training commitment. His running partner logged 15 miles separately. What was his weekly training commitment?

A student began with 125 problems. She subtracted 118 problems already mastered. She added 79 problems from a new chapter. She added 62 problems from additional practice. She multiplied by 9 for expected study time per problem. She added 18 hours for review sessions. She added 42 hours for final preparation (measured in total study hours). Throughout the term, she studied in the morning before school, afternoons in the library, and evenings at home, with study hours increasing as the exam approached. Her friend had 8 hours allocated (separate count). What was her total study hour allocation?
